findings.trigger_condition: edges contain a hashable value v and a distinct unhashable value u where v == u (e.g., a custom class with __hash__=None and __eq__ comparing equal to an int)
findings.root_cause: _id_of maintains two disjoint registries—hash_buckets for hashable values and unhashable_nodes for unhashable values. When an unhashable value u equal to an already-registered hashable value v is encountered, the except TypeError path scans only unhashable_nodes (which does not contain v) and assigns a new id, treating u and v as distinct nodes.
findings.impact: Equal values that should be merged into a single node are instead treated as separate nodes, producing an extra node in the output layers and incorrect dependency grouping. For example, dependency_layers([(1, 42), (2, SpecialInt(42))]) yields [[42, SpecialInt(42)], [1, 2]] instead of the correct [[42], [1, 2]].
findings.suggested_validation: Define a class with __eq__ returning True when compared to int 42 and __hash__=None. Call dependency_layers([(1, 42), (2, SpecialInt(42))]). Assert result == [[42], [1, 2]], confirming the two equal-valued nodes collapsed into one.

candidate-A.notes: Self-review of candidate-A. Reported only cross-hashability equal-value dedup miss; did not report unhashable registry O(N^2).
